land.text: Mecca, where in about 964 'the Egyptian ruler Abu al-Misk Kafur installed a Meccan sharif as emir to improve pilgrim safety'

predecessors.note: The Ikhshidids held the Hejaz (guardianship of Mecca and Medina) from 944; Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani turned to the Fatimids about 969 (ikhshidid-dynasty dossier). The sharifate page dates the state from about 967.

land.text: the Hejaz: in June 1916 'Hussein bin Ali, Sharif of Mecca, took the title of king of the Hejaz' as the Arab Revolt began on 10 June 1916

successors.note: Hussein held both offices, Sharif and King, from 1916 to 1924 (Arab Revolt page); the dossier ends the sharifate when the kingdom begins so the land is not drawn twice. The page ends the sharifate itself in 1925 with the kingdom (the surrender of Hussein's son Ali on 23 December 1925; the Kingdom of Hejaz page also gives 19 December).

rulers.title: Emir of Mecca

rulers.note: The page also has him declare himself caliph in 1012 and give the title up the same year.

rulers.name: Qatadah ibn Idris
rulers.title: Emir of Mecca
rulers.note: He 'seized power around 1200' and was recognised by the Ayyubid sultan; his descendants ruled until 1925.

rulers.name: Hussein bin Ali
rulers.title: Sharif and Emir of Mecca
rulers.note: Appointed by Abdul Hamid II in 1908; King of the Hejaz from June 1916. The page's list is partial, with gaps (1220-1788, 1836-1858, 1877-1882).

correction.text: Mecca and its surroundings, the seat of the first sharifs

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the state). The page 'does not give a precise founding territory'; its core cities are Mecca, Medina and Jeddah. The 40 km disc round Mecca is the researcher's, confidence 1; the Sulayhids occupied the Hejaz in 1062 and 'appointed the emirs of Mecca' for a time, and the Ayyubids sought sovereignty after 1171 (suzerain dossiers record those).

correction.text: the Hejaz under the Qatadid sharifs, from about 1200

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Qatadids ruled from about 1200 to 1925 under Ayyubid, Mamluk ('a regular province after 1350') and, from 1517, Ottoman suzerainty. The page's limits are for 'much of the 19th century' (Al-'Ula north, Al Lith south, 'never beyond the Khaybar oasis' east); they are used for the whole period by the researcher (confidence 1 before 1800). The gazetteer's Hejaz name resolves to the three provinces and is far larger (about 356,000 km2 by cells); the polygon trims it to about 170,000 km2.

correction.text: Mecca alone, after the Wahhabi conquest of the rest of the Hejaz; Sharif Ghalib 'returned as a Saudi vassal'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'In 1803 Wahhabis under Abdulaziz Al Saud attacked Mecca. Sharif Ghalib fled, then returned as a Saudi vassal' (the page also has the Wahhabis taking the two holy cities in 1801). Yahya (II) ibn Surur ruled 1803-1813. The 30 km disc is the researcher's.

correction.text: the Hejaz again from 1813, with Egyptian and then Ottoman garrisons

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Tusun Pasha took Mecca in 1813' and the Egyptian occupation lasted to 1840 (Convention of London); 'a dual system of emir and wali' governed under the Ottomans. The Hejaz is drawn whole because the sharif kept his office, but the muhammad-ali-dynasty dossier records the Hejaz as Egyptian until 27 November 1840. The limits are the page's for the 19th century.

ledger.note: c. 967: the sharifate begins. 'c. 964: the Egyptian ruler Abu al-Misk Kafur installed a Meccan sharif as emir to improve pilgrim safety'; the page dates the state from c. 967, when Ja'far ibn Muhammad ruled (967-980); Fatimid suzerainty from the conquest of Egypt in 969. Year dated 'c.' on the page.
c. 1200-1201: the Qatadids take the sharifate. 'Qatadah ibn Idris seized power around 1200 and was recognised as emir by the Ayyubid sultan. His descendants ruled until 1925.'

minus.text: the Hejaz of the sharifate's own keyframe (Makkah, Al Madinah and Tabuk within the Hejaz polygon), which the Habesh Eyalet's keyframe of 1557 draws whole

region.text: the Hejaz of the sharifate's own keyframe (Makkah, Al Madinah and Tabuk within the Hejaz polygon), which the Habesh Eyalet's keyframe of 1557 draws whole; without the Jeddah coast, which the Habesh Eyalet keeps (fx-54 E05)

ledger.note: 1557: the Habesh Eyalet is formed, and the habesh-eyalet dossier draws the whole Hejaz (a colony of the Ottoman Empire, which the compiler's colony rule 'R1' lets win against any other dossier), so this state held no cell from 1557 to 1802 and the Hejaz was drawn as Habesh. The Sharifate page: 'A dual system of government existed over Mecca for much of this period'; 'Ottoman authority was only indirect, as the arrangement left real power with the Emir'; 'When the Sharifs accepted Ottoman sovereignty, the Sultan confirmed them in their position as rulers of Mecca'; Mecca, Medina and Jeddah were its largest cities. The Habesh Eyalet page: the eyalet covered only the 'coastal Hejaz' and in 1829 Burckhardt called the pashalik of Jeddah 'reduced to perfect insignificance' by the power of the Sharif of Mecca. The state keeps its land as an Ottoman vassal (hierarchy.csv draws the tint). [fx-43 R099] The cause is in habesh-eyalet (kf 1557, ledger/0, kf 1865 and the successor land draw the whole Hejaz): see the handoff of fx-43. [orchestrator, 3 Nov 2026, fx-54 handoff: the Jeddah 50 km disc stays with habesh-eyalet, which now holds only the Jeddah coast.]

Mecca, where Sharif Ghalib returned as a Saudi vassal

ledger.note: 1803: the Wahhabis take the Hejaz. 'Wahhabis under Abdulaziz Al Saud attacked Mecca. Sharif Ghalib fled, then returned as a Saudi vassal' (Sharifate page); the Diriyah page has Saud sending forces 'to bring the region of Hejaz under his rule' in 1803, Taif first, then Mecca and Medina, undated. The Sharifate page also has 'in 1801 the Wahhabis took the two holy cities'.

minus.text: the Hejaz as the page bounds it for the 19th century: Mecca, Medina and Jeddah, north to Al-'Ula, south to Al Lith, east not beyond Khaybar
Mecca, where Sharif Ghalib returned as a Saudi vassal

ledger.note: 1813: the Hejaz returns. 'Tusun Pasha took Mecca in 1813', ending the Saudi hold; Ghalib ibn Masaad ruled again 1813-1827 (page list). The Egyptian occupation of the Hejaz is dated 1813-1840 on the page, with Ibrahim Pasha 'the nominal Ottoman ruler of the Hejaz from 1811 to 1840'.

10 June 1916: the Arab Revolt and the kingdom. 'The rebellion against the ruling Turks was officially initiated at Mecca on 10 June 1916'; 'in June 1916 Hussein bin Ali, Sharif of Mecca, took the title of king of the Hejaz'; the Allies recognised him only in that title. The page ends the sharifate itself in 1925.

wars.name: Wahhabi conquest of the Hejaz
wars.outcome: 1803 Mecca attacked; Ghalib fled and returned as a Saudi vassal; Taif first, then Mecca and Medina (Diriyah page); 1813 Tusun Pasha took Mecca.
wars.note: The war article (Ottoman-Saudi War) did not load under three titles; the Diriyah dossier carries 1802 Taif, 1803 Mecca, April 1804 Medina, January 1813 the loss of Mecca.

wars.name: Arab Revolt in the Hejaz
wars.outcome: 5 June 1916 the attack on Medina failed; 10 June the revolt was proclaimed at Mecca; Jeddah surrendered on 16 June; Mecca fell on 9 July; Ta'if on 22 September; Rabigh, Yanbu and al Qunfudhah by the end of September; Medina held out until 9 January 1919.
wars.note: The war continues under kingdom-of-hejaz, which carries the later events.

certainty.note: A holy-city emirate with no described boundary on the page: Mecca is firm; the Hejaz limits (Al-'Ula, Al Lith, Khaybar) are the page's for the 19th century only; suzerainty changed repeatedly (Ikhshidid, Fatimid, Sulayhid, Ayyubid, Rasulid, Mamluk, Ottoman, Saudi, Egyptian).

notes: State Cliopatria lacks (its Hejaz rows start with the Kingdom of Hejaz in 1916). Written by me-10-x; 5 pages opened (budget up to 5). Requested as a counterpart by ayyubid-sultanate, ikhshidid-dynasty, mamluk-beys-of-egypt, rasulid-dynasty and sulayhid-dynasty; their vassal events (944-969 Ikhshidid, 1062-1067 Sulayhid, 1174-1238 Ayyubid, 1238 Rasulid) are not mirrored here because the Sharifate page does not date them (it says only that the Sulayhids occupied the Hejaz in 1062 and appointed emirs 'for a time'). Not opened: Hejaz Vilayet, Emirate of Medina, the Ottoman-Saudi war article (three titles failed), Fatimid and Mamluk pages. The page's ruler list is partial (gaps 1220-1788, 1836-1858, 1877-1882). The dossier ends in June 1916 where the page ends in 1925, to avoid drawing the Hejaz twice (kingdom-of-hejaz covers June 1916-December 1925); the Hejaz of 1517-1803 and 1813-1916 is also recorded as directly Ottoman in the ottoman-empire dossier (a 1517-12 gain from the Mamluks), and the muhammad-ali-dynasty dossier holds it to 1840: the reviewer should decide whether the sharifate is drawn as a vassal tint under them or only as a caption. Page conflicts: Wahhabi capture of Mecca in 1801 (Sharifate page) or 1803 (same page, Diriyah page); Kingdom of Hejaz end 19 or 23 December 1925. The 1803-1812 Mecca disc and the polygon are the researcher's. Taif, Asir and Yemen are not claimed (the page is silent; Yemen it assigns to the Sulayhids in 1062).
